questions.prompt: Who maintains jmeter-plugins.org and the Plugins Manager?
options: A separate community project, not the Apache JMeter project
The Apache Software Foundation as part of core JMeter
Oracle
BlazeMeter only, and plugins are paid
questions.explanation: The plugins are third-party community components. They are free but not part of Apache JMeter itself.

questions.prompt: Where do you find installed plugins' jars?
options: lib/ext (and their dependencies in lib)
bin/templates
docs/
The user's Downloads folder
questions.explanation: Plugins Manager installs component jars into lib/ext and libraries into lib.

questions.prompt: You must restart JMeter after installing plugins with the Plugins Manager.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The manager applies changes and restarts JMeter so the new classes load.

questions.prompt: What advantage does the Concurrency Thread Group have over the standard Thread Group?
options: It targets a concurrency level with ramp-up steps and hold time, and can work with the Throughput Shaping Timer's feedback function
It is faster because it uses no threads
It is the only group that supports HTTP
It records scripts
questions.explanation: It is designed for target concurrency with steps and holds, and integrates with __tstFeedback. It still uses threads.

questions.prompt: How do you make CI agents install the same plugins as your laptop?
options: Use the Plugins Manager command line (PluginsManagerCMD install ... or install-for-jmx) in the build, pinned to versions
Copy your entire laptop JMeter folder by USB
Ask each tester to click Install
Plugins work without installation on CI
questions.explanation: Scripted installs with pinned versions are reproducible. Manual steps drift.

questions.prompt: Which practices apply to plugins? Select all that apply.
options: Only add plugins you need
Record plugin names and versions with the test
Check a plugin is maintained and compatible with your JMeter version
Install every available plugin just in case
questions.explanation: Each plugin is a dependency and a compatibility risk. Installing everything slows start-up and complicates upgrades.

questions.prompt: A .jmx opens with `CannotResolveClassException: kg.apc.jmeter.threads.UltimateThreadGroup` on a teammate's machine. What is the fix?
options: Install the Custom Thread Groups plugin (jpgc-casutg) on that machine, ideally via the Plugins Manager's 'install-for-jmx'
Upgrade Java
Delete the thread group in a text editor
Increase the heap
questions.explanation: kg.apc classes come from jmeter-plugins; Ultimate Thread Group is in Custom Thread Groups. Java or heap changes do not add missing classes.

questions.prompt: You need 'step 100 users every 2 minutes up to 500, hold 10 minutes'. Which choice is cleanest?
options: Concurrency Thread Group with Target Concurrency 500, Ramp Up Time 10 min, Ramp-Up Steps Count 5, Hold 10 min
Five standard Thread Groups started by hand
One standard Thread Group with 500 threads and 600 s ramp-up
A Synchronizing Timer of 100
questions.explanation: The Concurrency Thread Group models stepped load directly. A linear ramp-up is not stepped, manual starts are error-prone, and a synchronizing timer creates bursts.

coding.title: Stepped concurrency schedule
coding.prompt:
Model the Concurrency Thread Group. Write `target_at(target, ramp_s, steps, hold_s, t)` returning the target concurrency at second `t`:

- During ramp-up (`t < ramp_s`) concurrency rises in `steps` equal steps: step `k = t // (ramp_s / steps)` (0-based) gives `round(target * (k + 1) / steps)`.
- From `ramp_s` until `ramp_s + hold_s` (exclusive) it is `target`.
- After that it is `0`.

Example: `target_at(500, 600, 5, 600, 0)` is `100`; at `t=130` it is `200`.
coding.explanation: Working out the schedule before the run lets you check the generator can hold the peak and lets you line up result graphs with each step.
hints: Use integer division to get the current step.
Handle the hold and the end separately.

coding.title: Detect missing plugin classes
coding.prompt: Write `plugin_classes(jmx_text)` returning a sorted list of distinct class names in the .jmx XML that come from jmeter-plugins (they start with `kg.apc.`). Classes appear in attributes like `guiclass="kg.apc.jmeter.threads.UltimateThreadGroupGui"` or `testclass="kg.apc.jmeter.threads.UltimateThreadGroup"`.
coding.explanation: A quick scan of the .jmx for plugin classes tells you which plugins a plan needs before it fails on another machine; the Plugins Manager's install-for-jmx does the same thing.
hints: Use `re.findall` on quoted values starting with `kg.apc.`.

tests.name: No plugins
tests.code:
assert plugin_classes('<TestPlan guiclass="TestPlanGui"/>') == []
assert plugin_classes('<a testclass="kg.apc.X"/>') == ['kg.apc.X']
